symptom: check flagged `trim($v) != empty` (E015) but said nothing about `$v != empty and trim($v) != ''` (the empty half is dead) or `$v != empty and $v != ''` (lets '   ' through as text) — the far more common blank checks (ako/mxcli#2566, mendixlabs/mxcli#1937).
cause: E015 looks at one comparison against `empty`; it deliberately skips the and-ed idiom (chainComparesWithBlank) and nothing judged the chain as a whole.
fix: Per and-chain (or-chain with =): a `<x> != empty` operand beside `f(<x>, …) != ''` with f in neverEmptyStringFuncs is E016 (info, redundant); beside `<x> != ''` is E017 (info, trim missing). Same operand by exprKey, same chain only.
insight: Judge an idiom at the chain level, not at the comparison: flattenChain + exprKey already gave the shape E015 needed to skip, and the same pair of helpers finds the two adjacent idioms. Info, not warning, because both build and the first behaves correctly — Studio Pro-authored projects are full of the redundant form.
test: mdl/exprcheck/blank_guard_2566_test.go (9 positive shapes incl. or-chains and reversed order, 7 controls: unmeasured function, other operand, other chain, `or` with !=); all positives failed before; live: check -p on TestApp reports E016 and E017 at info, nothing on trim($v) != ''
